questions.title: How does the Federal Circuit distinguish between questions of law and fact in DuPont factor analysis?
questions.question_body: In the opinion, the court states that 'Likelihood of confusion is a question of law, based on findings of relevant underlying facts, namely findings under the DuPont factors.' However, it also says 'Each of the [thirteen] DuPont factors presents a question of fact.' I am confused about how the court applies de novo review to the likelihood of confusion conclusion while reviewing the DuPont factor findings for substantial evidence. Can someone clarify how these standards interact in practice?

questions.title: Can 'credit card services' and 'banking services' be considered 'legally identical' if one party doesn't offer credit cards?
questions.question_body: Apex Bank does not offer credit cards, only banking and financing services. However, the Board found the parties' services to be 'legally identical, in part.' The court affirmed this finding under DuPont Factor 2. How can services be legally identical when one party's business model (issuing credit cards via a bank partner) differs from the other's (direct banking services), especially when Apex explicitly stated they do not offer credit cards?

questions.title: Why must the scope of third-party marks in DuPont Factor 6 match the scope of goods similarity in Factor 2?
questions.question_body: The court vacated the Board's Factor 6 analysis because the Board limited third-party marks to 'credit card services' while Factor 2 found 'banking and financing services' to be highly similar. The court stated, 'When the Board has already made a factual finding that the services are highly similar... the Board should retain the same scope in its consideration of similarity under the other factors.' Is there a specific doctrine requiring this consistency, or is this a general principle of administrative law?

questions.title: Does a remand on DuPont Factor 6 automatically require a remand on Factor 1 regarding commercial impression?
questions.question_body: The court vacated Factor 1 (similarity of marks) solely because reconsideration of Factor 6 (third-party marks) 'may result in a different determination of the mark's commercial strength or weakness and affect the overall commercial impression.' Is there a binding precedent that links the strength of a mark (Factor 6) directly to the commercial impression analysis (Factor 1) in this manner?

questions.title: What is the proper methodology for defining services when a Trademark ID Manual entry has been deleted?
questions.question_body: The Board noted that the entry for 'credit card services' was deleted from the Trademark ID Manual after CC Serve's registration. Consequently, the Board used dictionary definitions to define the services. Is this the standard approach for defining goods and services in an opposition proceeding when the official manual classification has changed or been removed?

questions.title: What is the quantitative threshold for a 'crowded field' defense under DuPont Factor 6?
questions.question_body: The Board rejected Apex's argument that CC Serve's mark was weak because there were only nine Aspire-formative marks for credit card services. The court cited cases where 14 or 26 marks were considered 'considerable.' Is there a specific numerical threshold established in Federal Circuit case law for determining when a field is 'crowded' enough to demonstrate mark weakness?
